title: Frame geometry of split torus torsors
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], $S$ a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme], and $r\geq0$. Put $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$, with $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$. Let $q:Y\to S$ be faithfully flat and of finite presentation [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], with a right $T$-action over $S$ such that $(y,t)\mapsto(y,yt)$ identifies $Y\times_kT$ with $Y\times_SY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. There are invertible $\mathcal O_S$-modules $A_1,\ldots,A_r$ [def-sc-invertible-module] and a $T$-equivariant $S$-isomorphism
$$Y\simeq A_1^\times\times_S\cdots\times_S A_r^\times.$$
Here $A_i^\times$ is the scheme representing $U\mapsto\operatorname{Isom}_{\mathcal O_U}(\mathcal O_U,f^*A_i)$ on $S$-schemes $f:U\to S$, with scalar action on frames; pullbacks are tensor inverse images [def-pc-module-pullback]. Set $Y_0=S$ and $Y_j=\prod_{i=1}^j A_i^\times$ for $1\leq j\leq r$, with $q_j:Y_j\to Y_{j-1}$ forgetting the last frame and $f_{j-1}:Y_{j-1}\to S$ the projection. Write $B_j=f_{j-1}^*(A_j^\vee)$, where $A_j^\vee=\mathcal Hom(A_j,\mathcal O_S)$. For the rank-two projective bundle
$$p_j:P_j=\mathbf P_{Y_{j-1}}(\mathcal O_{Y_{j-1}}\oplus B_j)\to Y_{j-1}$$
in the quotient convention [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry, def-amb-finite-locally-free-module], there is an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] $i_j:Y_j\hookrightarrow P_j$ with $p_ji_j=q_j$. Its image is the locus where both summand maps of the universal quotient are isomorphisms. The first summand gives an isomorphism $\mathcal O_{Y_j}\simeq i_j^*\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)$. If $S$ is smooth separated and of finite type over $k$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], with separated meaning that the diagonal is a closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion], then every $Y_j$ and $P_j$ is also smooth separated and of finite type over $k$. The isomorphism $Y\simeq Y_r$ identifies $q$ with $q_1\circ\cdots\circ q_r$, and for $r=0$ it identifies $q$ with $\mathrm{id}_S$.

proof.text: The singleton $\{q:Y\to S\}$ is an fppf covering by the flatness, surjectivity and finite-presentation hypotheses and [def-pc-fppf-site]. Apply [lem-trf-fppf-covering-is-fpqc] to get an fpqc covering. The given torsor isomorphism defines a morphism $g:Y\times_SY\to T$ by $z=y g(y,z)$. On the triple fibre product, uniqueness in that isomorphism and associativity of the action give $g(y,w)=g(y,z)g(z,w)$; also $g(y,y)=1$. Thus each coordinate $g_i$ is an invertible regular function with $g_{i,13}=g_{i,12}g_{i,23}$. These are identities of scheme morphisms, as seen by applying the given isomorphism, not merely identities on field-valued points.

source.place: Tags 0499 (lemma-characterize-trivial-pseudo-torsors) and 049A (definition-principal-homogeneous-space); fpqc covering from topologies.tex Tag 022C (lemma-zariski-etale-smooth-syntomic-fppf-fpqc)

proof.text: On $\mathcal O_Y$ use the descent isomorphism $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\mathcal O_Y\to\operatorname{pr}_2^*\mathcal O_Y$ given by multiplication by $g_i^{-1}$. Step 1 proves its cocycle. Apply the equivalence and invertible-module clause of [lem-pc-fpqc-descent] to obtain an invertible module $A_i$ and a trivialization $\theta_i:q^*A_i\simeq\mathcal O_Y$ respecting that datum. Put $e_i=\theta_i^{-1}(1)$, a frame of $q^*A_i$. On $Y\times_SY$ the compatibility is $\theta_{i,z}(v)=g_i(y,z)^{-1}\theta_{i,y}(v)$, equivalently $e_i(z)=g_i(y,z)e_i(y)$ in the common pulled-back line. This choice of inverse in the descent map therefore gives the scalar action on frames requested in the statement.

For any invertible module $A$ on a scheme $V$, form $P=\mathbf P_V(\mathcal O_V\oplus A^\vee)$ using [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. Let $W\subset P$ be the locus where both summand maps $\alpha:\mathcal O_P\to\mathcal O_P(1)$ and $\beta:p^*A^\vee\to\mathcal O_P(1)$ are isomorphisms. It is open: in local bases each map is multiplication by one function, and its invertibility locus is the principal open where that function is a unit. The quotient classification identifies maps $h:U\to W$ over $V$ with frames of $h^*A$: normalize the quotient by $\alpha^{-1}$, obtaining $(1,\alpha^{-1}\beta):\mathcal O_U\oplus h^*A^\vee\to\mathcal O_U$. Its second component is evaluation at a unique frame $e:\mathcal O_U\simeq h^*A$. In a basis this is just the correspondence $u\in\mathcal O_U^\times\leftrightarrow(b\mapsto ub)$; it also proves the inverse correspondence, independently of the basis. These operations commute with pullback. Thus $W$ represents $A^\times$ with its scalar action. Its inclusion into $P$ is the required open immersion, and $\alpha$ gives $\mathcal O_W\simeq\mathcal O_P(1)|_W$. Over any open trivializing $A$, the quotient classification identifies $P$ with $\mathbf P^1_V$ and $W$ with $D_+(T_0)\cap D_+(T_1)$; the coordinates are $u=T_1/T_0$ and $u^{-1}=T_0/T_1$. In particular $W$ is locally $\operatorname{Spec}R[u,u^{-1}]$.

source.place: Tag 01OB (definition-projective-bundle), subsequent quotient-functor discussion; Tag 01OE (lemma-projective-space-bundle); standard affine homogeneous-localization charts

proof.text: The frames $e_i$ from step 2 and the representing property in step 3 give an $S$-morphism $\phi:Y\to F=\prod_{i=1}^r A_i^\times$. Pull back along $q:Y\to S$. Trivializing the lines by $e_i(y)$ identifies $F\times_SY$ with $T\times_kY$; the pullback of $\phi$ sends $(z,y)$ to $(g(y,z),y)$. Its inverse sends $(t,y)$ to $(yt,y)$, by the assumed torsor isomorphism. The inverse is compatible with the canonical descent data: the base change of $\phi$ is compatible, and inverting the equality expressing its compatibility gives the corresponding equality for its inverse. By [lem-galois-fpqc-morphisms-descend] that inverse descends uniquely to $F\to Y$, and faithfulness in the same statement makes the two composites identities. Hence $\phi$ is an isomorphism. Applying step 2 to $(y,yt)$ gives $e_i(yt)=t_i e_i(y)$, so $\phi$ is $T$-equivariant. If $r=0$, $F=S$, the base-changed map is the given diagonal isomorphism $Y\simeq Y\times_SY$, and the same inverse descent proves that $\phi=q:Y\simeq S$.

source.place: Tag 02W0 (lemma-refine-coverings-fully-faithful), final assertion, applied to the fpqc singleton q; groupoids.tex Tag 0499

proof.text: Define $Y_j$ by the first $j$ frame factors. For a test scheme $U\to Y_{j-1}$, its maps to $Y_j$ are exactly frames of the pullback of $A_j$ along $U\to S$, by [def-pc-fibre-product] and [def-pc-module-pullback]. The pullback-dual identification $f_{j-1}^*(A_j^\vee)\simeq(f_{j-1}^*A_j)^\vee$ is the identity on coefficients in every local rank-one basis; those identities agree when the basis is multiplied by a unit. Apply the construction and the explicit quotient of step 3 to the line $f_{j-1}^*A_j$. This gives exactly $P_j$, $i_j$, its image, and its first-summand trivialization. The universal property of the fibre product says that the successive forgetful maps compose to the structure map $Y_r\to S$. Together with step 4 this proves the stated factorization of $q$, including the empty composite when $r=0$.

source.place: Tag 01OB (definition-projective-bundle), quotient-functor discussion; applying the rank-one quotient calculation of step 3

proof.text: Assume now that $S$ is smooth separated and of finite type over $k$. Choose a finite affine open cover $U_a=\operatorname{Spec}R_a$ simultaneously trivializing $A_1,\ldots,A_r$. Such a cover exists by local rank-one freeness [def-sc-invertible-module] and quasi-compactness of $S$ [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; refine to affine opens, rather than assuming intersections of affine opens are affine. Each $R_a$ is a finitely generated $k$-algebra. Step 3 and the product description identify $Y_j|_{U_a}$ with $\operatorname{Spec}R_a[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_j^{\pm1}]$, and $P_j|_{U_a}$ with $\mathbf P^1_{Y_{j-1}|_{U_a}}$. Its two affine charts have rings $R_a[u_1^{\pm1},\ldots,u_{j-1}^{\pm1},v]$. Indeed the degree-zero localization of $R[T_0,T_1]$ at $T_0$ is $R[T_1/T_0]$, with inverse sending the free variable to that ratio, and likewise at $T_1$ [def-nagata-relative-projective-space]. All these rings are finite type over $k$: adjoin finitely many variables and their inverses with relations $u_iw_i=1$. These finitely many affine charts cover the schemes, which proves finite type by its definition. This includes $Y_0=S$ and the empty base.

source.place: Tags 01OB and 01OE, two standard projective-line charts; morphisms.tex Section 01T0, definition of finite type

proof.text: Every $U_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ in step 6 is smooth by [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. The Laurent-coordinate charts of $Y_j|_{U_a}$ are opens in $\mathbf A^j_{U_a}$, and those of $P_j|_{U_a}$ are opens in $\mathbf A^j_{U_a}$ as well (there are $j-1$ Laurent coordinates and one polynomial coordinate). Their projections to $U_a$ are smooth by [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] and open restriction [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-restrict-open-subschemes]. Composing with $U_a\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth by [lem-trf-smooth-composition]. These charts cover $Y_j$ and $P_j$, so [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-local-on-source] proves their smoothness over $k$.

source.place: Tags 01V6 (lemma-smooth-characterize), 01VA (lemma-composition-smooth); polynomial smoothness from algebra.tex Tag 00T7

proof.text: The projection $p_j:P_j\to Y_{j-1}$ is separated by [lem-trf-projective-bundle-quotient-geometry]. The diagonal of its restriction $q_j$ to the open $Y_j\subset P_j$ is the base change of $\Delta_{p_j}$ along $Y_j\times_{Y_{j-1}}Y_j\to P_j\times_{Y_{j-1}}P_j$, so it is a closed immersion by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change]. To compose separated maps $X\xrightarrow f B\xrightarrow h C$, factor $\Delta_{hf}$ as $X\xrightarrow{\Delta_f}X\times_BX\to X\times_CX$. The second map is the base change of $\Delta_h$, so both maps and their composite are closed immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-base-change, lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-comp]. Starting with the assumed separated map $S\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, induction therefore proves that every $Y_j$ and $P_j$ is separated over $k$.
